sections.html:
West Haven is a city in Weber County, about 35 miles north of Salt Lake City and west of the Wasatch Mountains. It borders Ogden to the east, Roy to the south, Hooper to the west and Marriott-Slaterville to the north.

The Weber and Ogden Rivers meet in the northeastern part of the city, and the elevation is about 4,269 feet. West Haven belongs to the Ogden-Clearfield metropolitan area, so many residents commute to jobs in Ogden, Roy and Davis County.

The city is young on paper and old on the map. It was incorporated on July 1, 1991, by combining the unincorporated communities of Kanesville and Wilson. The street grid, the farmhouses and the newer subdivisions all sit inside one set of city limits, which is why two West Haven houses can sell very differently.

sections.h2: How did Kanesville and Wilson become West Haven?
sections.html:
Both communities were farming settlements first. Wilson was formed in 1854 and named for four Wilson brothers who started farming there that year. John Martin moved from Ogden in 1856 and was the first to settle west of the Weber River, and an irrigation company formed in 1879.

Kanesville was first settled in 1868 as Northwest Hooper and was later named for Thomas L. Kane when a ward was organized in 1882. Kanesville Elementary still carries the old name.

The city installed a citywide sewer system in 2002, which opened the door to denser building. Wikipedia lists the population at 2,172 in 1990, 3,976 in 2000, 10,272 in 2010 and 16,739 in 2020, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate quoted at the top of this page is 25,627.

sections.h2: What do the seasons mean for a house near Ogden?
sections.html:
West Haven has four real seasons, with hot summers and cold winters. Climate normals for nearby Ogden show an average July high of 91.3 degrees and a January low of 21.2 degrees, with about 16.4 inches of precipitation a year.

Ogden's record low is minus 23 degrees and its record high is 106 degrees. Snow usually begins in late October or early November and ends around April.

That swing is hard on a few parts of a house:

  • Roofs and gutters that hold snow and ice.
  • Exposed pipes and sprinkler lines that can freeze.
  • Furnaces, which carry a heavy load for half the year.
  • Driveways and flatwork that crack as the ground freezes and thaws.

A buyer's inspector will check each of these, and a heating system near the end of its life is a frequent point of negotiation.

sections.h2: What is daily life like in West Haven?
sections.html:
West Haven is a fully urban city by the census definition, yet it keeps some farm character. The Kanesville Elementary profile describes mostly single-family neighborhoods, more condominiums and multifamily buildings being added, and 19th-century farmhouses and working farms that raise crops and animals.

The city bought 40 acres for a park in 1994, and the site has playground equipment, sports fields and a historical marker. Plans call for a River Parkway Trail with a fishing bridge and a pedestrian tunnel under 21st Street that would link to the Weber County Centennial Trail. City committees cover trails and parks, beautification and historic preservation, and the city runs its own arena and park reservations.

For a seller, that mix matters. A house near the new trails and schools reaches families, while a house on a larger rural lot reaches buyers who want space for animals or outbuildings.

West Haven is served by the Weber School District, which covers all of Weber County except Ogden City. Schools in or near the city include Country View Elementary, Haven Bay Elementary, Kanesville Elementary and West Haven Elementary.

Rocky Mountain Junior High and the newer Mountain View Junior High are in West Haven. Kanesville Elementary's feeder pattern runs to Rocky Mountain Junior High and then to Fremont High School in Plain City. Kanesville opened in 1977, and the district lists about 750 students there.

Two of the elementary and junior high buildings opened as recently as 2024, which tells you how fast the city has added families. Buyers with children often ask which school a house feeds, so confirm the boundary with the district before you advertise it.

sections.h2: What city rules and permits come up when selling in West Haven?
sections.html:
West Haven's Community Development group covers the Building Department, business licensing, code enforcement and emergency management. City offices are at 4150 S 3900 W, and the main line is 801-731-4519.

A summary of the city's permit requirements says residential permits are needed for new houses, additions, remodels and basement finishing, and that fire sprinklers and alarms go through the Weber Fire District. Applications and inspection requests run through the CityInspect portal. The same summary lists a 7 to 14 working day review for residential permits, but it also says requirements change, so confirm with the city.

Before you list, run through a short checklist:

  • Finished basements, decks or sheds should have permits on file.
  • Open code complaints should be cleared with city code enforcement.
  • Utility accounts, including the West Haven Special Service District bill, should be current.

sections.h2: How do property tax and recording work in Weber County?
sections.html:
Weber County bills property tax once a year and the payment is due November 30. The county's 2026 calendar shows tax notices mailed on October 17, valuation notices around July 20 and an appeal deadline of September 15. Unpaid taxes become delinquent on December 1, and penalties and interest follow.

Utah gives a primary residence a 45% exemption, so tax applies to 55% of market value. In Weber County the home must be the occupant's main home for at least 183 consecutive days in a year, and a tenant's primary residence can qualify as well. Nightly rentals, vacation homes and second homes do not. If the county mails a declaration form and you do not return it within 30 days, the exemption is removed. Call the Assessor at (801) 399-8572 if you are unsure of your status.

Deeds are recorded at the Weber County Recorder, 2380 Washington Blvd, Suite 370, Ogden. Fees changed on May 6, 2026: $45.00 for the first page, nothing for additional standard pages, and $2.00 for each description over ten. Property tax is prorated by the title company at closing.

sections.h2: What are your options for selling a West Haven house?
sections.html:
West Haven owners can list with an agent, sell on their own or ask for a cash offer, and the right choice depends on the condition of the house and how much time you have. The condition of the house, the roof and the heating system usually drive what a buyer will pay.

Cash Home Buyers buys houses in Utah as they stand. Owners who contact us usually have a reason to move quickly, such as a job change, an inherited house, a tenant they want to be done with or a mortgage they are behind on. We look at the property and explain what a sale would involve, and you choose whether to go ahead.

sections.h2: What do West Haven sellers often face?
sections.html:
• Competition from newly built houses in a city that has grown by tens of percent in a few years.
  • Older farmhouses and rural lots where the land and the house are valued differently.
  • Primary residence exemption questions when a house is converted to a rental.
  • Out-of-state heirs who need to sort out a deed and a recording before anything else.

faqs.q: What county is West Haven, UT in?
faqs.a: West Haven is in Weber County. Property tax, deeds and valuation appeals all go through Weber County offices in Ogden.

faqs.q: When is property tax due in West Haven?
faqs.a: Weber County's due date is November 30. Unpaid taxes are delinquent on December 1, and the county's calendar shows interest beginning February 1 on the prior year's delinquent balance.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Weber County?
faqs.a: The Recorder lists $45.00 for the first page, with no charge for additional standard pages and $2.00 for each legal description over ten, effective May 6, 2026.

faqs.q: Which school district covers West Haven?
faqs.a: The Weber School District serves West Haven. Elementary schools nearby include Country View, Haven Bay, Kanesville and West Haven Elementary, with Rocky Mountain and Mountain View junior highs.

faqs.q: Can I sell a West Haven house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. You are not required to fix a house before selling it, and a cash sale to a buyer who takes the property in its present condition is one way to skip repairs.
